question: A population falls by 12% in the first year. By what percentage must it increase in the second year so that at the end of the second year the population is exactly the same as the original?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To restore a value after a **percentage decrease**, use the formula:

Required Increase % = [r ÷ (100 − r)] × 100, where r is the **percentage fall**.

Required Increase % = [12 ÷ (100 − 12)] × 100

Required Increase % = (12 ÷ 88) × 100 ≈ 13.63%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First year **population decrease** = 12%.

**Formula Used:** Percentage Increase = (Change ÷ Initial Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/deb606c52a657af8cc65f004b51249ebae6031ffb64852d8df65552e9f715a5b.png] 

⇒ Let the **original population** be 100.

⇒ Population after 1st year = 100 − (12% of 100) = 100 − 12 = 88.

⇒ To return to 100, the **increase needed** = 100 − 88 = 12.

⇒ **Percentage increase** required on the new base (88) = (12 ÷ 88) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (3 ÷ 22) × 100 = 300 ÷ 22

⇒ Percentage increase = 13.6363...

**∴ The correct answer is 13.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Reversal Rule

If a value decreases by x%, the percentage increase required to restore the original value is [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100.

Base Change Principle

Percentage values change when the **base value** changes. Here, the first change is calculated on 100, while the second must be calculated on 88.

Reciprocal Ratios

Common restoration pairs: a 20% decrease requires a 25% increase; a 25% decrease requires a 33.33% increase; a 50% decrease requires a 100% increase.</p
